```kotlin
package com.example.bankingapp.viewmodel

import androidx.lifecycle.ViewModel
import androidx.lifecycle.viewModelScope
import com.example.bankingapp.data.fake.FakeBankingRepository
import com.example.bankingapp.data.model.Account
import com.example.bankingapp.data.model.Transaction
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.MutableStateFlow
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.StateFlow
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.asStateFlow
import kotlinx.coroutines.launch

data class BankingUiState(
    val isLoading: Boolean = false,
    val accounts: List<Account> = emptyList(),
    val selectedAccount: Account? = null,
    val transactions: List<Transaction> = emptyList(),
    val errorMessage: String? = null
)

class BankingViewModel : ViewModel() {

    private val repository = FakeBankingRepository()

    private val _uiState = MutableStateFlow(BankingUiState(isLoading = true))
    val uiState: StateFlow<BankingUiState> = _uiState.asStateFlow()

    init {
        loadAccounts()
    }

    fun loadAccounts() {
        viewModelScope.launch {
            _uiState.value = _uiState.value.copy(isLoading = true, errorMessage = null)
            try {
                val accounts = repository.getAccounts()
                val selected = accounts.firstOrNull()
                val tx = selected?.let { repository.getTransactions(it.id) }.orEmpty()

                _uiState.value = BankingUiState(
                    isLoading = false,
                    accounts = accounts,
                    selectedAccount = selected,
                    transactions = tx
                )
            } catch (e: Exception) {
                _uiState.value = _uiState.value.copy(
                    isLoading = false,
                    errorMessage = "Failed to load accounts"
                )
            }
        }
    }

    fun selectAccount(account: Account) {
        viewModelScope.launch {
            _uiState.value = _uiState.value.copy(isLoading = true, errorMessage = null)
            try {
                val tx = repository.getTransactions(account.id)
                _uiState.value = _uiState.value.copy(
                    isLoading = false,
                    selectedAccount = account,
                    transactions = tx
                )
            } catch (e: Exception) {
                _uiState.value = _uiState.value.copy(
                    isLoading = false,
                    errorMessage = "Failed to load transactions"
                )
            }
        }
    }
}
```

```kotlin
package com.example.bankingapp.ui

import androidx.compose.foundation.clickable
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.*
import androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.LazyColumn
import androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.items
import androidx.compose.material3.*
import androidx.compose.runtime.*
import androidx.compose.ui.Modifier
import androidx.compose.ui.unit.dp
import com.example.bankingapp.data.model.Account
import com.example.bankingapp.data.model.Transaction
import com.example.bankingapp.viewmodel.BankingViewModel

@Composable
fun BankingHomeScreen(viewModel: BankingViewModel) {
    val state by viewModel.uiState.collectAsState()

    Scaffold(
        topBar = {
            TopAppBar(title = { Text("My Bank") })
        }
    ) { padding ->
        Column(
            modifier = Modifier
                .padding(padding)
                .fillMaxSize()
                .padding(16.dp)
        ) {
            if (state.isLoading) {
                LinearProgressIndicator(modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth())
                Spacer(modifier = Modifier.height(16.dp))
            }

            state.errorMessage?.let {
                Text(text = it, color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.error)
                Spacer(modifier = Modifier.height(12.dp))
            }

            Text(
                text = "Accounts",
                style = MaterialTheme.typography.titleMedium
            )
            Spacer(modifier = Modifier.height(8.dp))

            state.accounts.forEach { account ->
                AccountCard(
                    account = account,
                    selected = account.id == state.selectedAccount?.id,
                    onClick = { viewModel.selectAccount(account) }
                )
                Spacer(modifier = Modifier.height(8.dp))
            }

            Spacer(modifier = Modifier.height(16.dp))

            Text(
                text = "Transactions",
                style = MaterialTheme.typography.titleMedium
            )
            Spacer(modifier = Modifier.height(8.dp))

            LazyColumn {
                items(state.transactions) { tx ->
                    TransactionRow(transaction = tx)
                    Divider()
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

@Composable
fun AccountCard(
    account: Account,
    selected: Boolean,
    onClick: () -> Unit
) {
    Card(
        modifier = Modifier
            .fillMaxWidth()
            .clickable(onClick = onClick)
    ) {
        Column(modifier = Modifier.padding(16.dp)) {
            Text(text = account.accountName, style = MaterialTheme.typography.titleMedium)
            Text(text = account.accountNumberMasked)
            Text(
                text = "${account.currency} %.2f".format(account.balance),
                style = MaterialTheme.typography.bodyLarge
            )
            if (selected) {
                Spacer(modifier = Modifier.height(4.dp))
                Text(text = "Selected", color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.primary)
            }
        }
    }
}

@Composable
fun TransactionRow(transaction: Transaction) {
    val sign = if (transaction.isDebit) "-" else "+"
    val amountText = "$sign%.2f".format(transaction.amount)

    Row(
        modifier = Modifier
            .fillMaxWidth()
            .padding(vertical = 12.dp),
        horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.SpaceBetween
    ) {
        Column {
            Text(text = transaction.description, style = MaterialTheme.typography.bodyLarge)
            Text(text = transaction.date, style = MaterialTheme.typography.bodySmall)
        }
        Text(
            text = amountText,
            color = if (transaction.isDebit) MaterialTheme.colorScheme.error else MaterialTheme.colorScheme.primary
        )
    }
}
```

Below is a **minimal Manifest V3 browser extension** that blocks a few common tracking scripts/requests using `declarativeNetRequest`.

It is intentionally small and safe to start with. You can expand the rules later.

## `manifest.json`

```json

  "manifest_version": 3,
  "name": "Privacy Blocker",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "description": "Blocks common tracking scripts and requests.",
  "permissions": ["declarativeNetRequest"],
  "host_permissions": ["<all_urls>"],
  "background": {
    "service_worker": "background.js"
  },
  "declarative_net_request": {
    "rule_resources": [
      {
        "id": "ruleset_1",
        "enabled": true,
        "path": "rules.json"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

```rust
use std::io::{self, Read, BufReader};

const BUF_SIZE: usize = 64 * 1024;

/// Trait for processing parsed records without storing them all in memory.
trait RecordHandler {
    fn handle_record(&mut self, record: &str);
}

/// Example handler: counts lines and bytes.
struct StatsHandler {
    records: u64,
    bytes: u64,
}

impl StatsHandler {
    fn new() -> Self {
        Self { records: 0, bytes: 0 }
    }
}

impl RecordHandler for StatsHandler {
    fn handle_record(&mut self, record: &str) {
        self.records += 1;
        self.bytes += record.len() as u64;
    }
}

/// Streaming parser: reads from an input stream in fixed-size buffers,
/// splits on newline boundaries, and processes one record at a time.
fn parse_stream<R: Read, H: RecordHandler>(reader: R, handler: &mut H) -> io::Result<()> {
    let mut reader = BufReader::with_capacity(BUF_SIZE, reader);
    let mut buf = Vec::with_capacity(BUF_SIZE);
    let mut chunk = [0u8; BUF_SIZE];

    loop {
        let n = reader.read(&mut chunk)?;
        if n == 0 {
            // Flush final partial record if present.
            if !buf.is_empty() {
                let record = std::str::from_utf8(&buf).unwrap_or("");
                handler.handle_record(record);
            }
            break;
        }

        for &b in &chunk[..n] {
            if b == b'\n' {
                let record = std::str::from_utf8(&buf).unwrap_or("");
                handler.handle_record(record);
                buf.clear();
            } else if b != b'\r' {
                buf.push(b);
            }
        }
    }

    Ok(())
}

fn main() -> io::Result<()> {
    let stdin = io::stdin();
    let mut handler = StatsHandler::new();

    parse_stream(stdin.lock(), &mut handler)?;

    eprintln!("records = {}, bytes = {}", handler.records, handler.bytes);
    Ok(())
}
```

```python
from collections import deque
import math
import statistics
import time


class MovingAverageFilter:
    def __init__(self, window_size=8):
        self.window = deque(maxlen=window_size)

    def update(self, value):
        self.window.append(value)
        return sum(self.window) / len(self.window)


class AccelerometerPipeline:
    def __init__(self, feature_window=50, anomaly_zscore_threshold=3.0):
        self.mag_filter = MovingAverageFilter(window_size=8)
        self.feature_history = deque(maxlen=feature_window)
        self.anomaly_zscore_threshold = anomaly_zscore_threshold

    def process_sample(self, ax, ay, az):
        # Step 1: compute magnitude
        magnitude = math.sqrt(ax * ax + ay * ay + az * az)

        # Step 2: filter magnitude
        filtered_mag = self.mag_filter.update(magnitude)

        # Step 3: store feature history
        self.feature_history.append(filtered_mag)

        # Not enough data to decide yet
        if len(self.feature_history) < 10:
            return {
                "anomaly": False,
                "magnitude": magnitude,
                "filtered_magnitude": filtered_mag,
                "zscore": 0.0,
            }

        # Step 4: compute rolling statistics
        mean_val = statistics.mean(self.feature_history)
        stdev_val = statistics.pstdev(self.feature_history)

        # Avoid divide-by-zero
        if stdev_val < 1e-6:
            zscore = 0.0
        else:
            zscore = abs(filtered_mag - mean_val) / stdev_val

        anomaly = zscore > self.anomaly_zscore_threshold

        return {
            "anomaly": anomaly,
            "magnitude": magnitude,
            "filtered_magnitude": filtered_mag,
            "mean": mean_val,
            "stdev": stdev_val,
            "zscore": zscore,
        }


# Example sensor read function

    Returns ax, ay, az in g or m/s^2 consistently.
    """
    # Dummy data with a periodic spike to simulate anomaly
    t = time.time()
    ax = 0.02 * math.sin(t)
    ay = 0.02 * math.cos(t)
    az = 1.0

    # Inject anomaly occasionally
    if int(t) % 20 == 0:
        ax += 3.0
        ay += 2.5

    return ax, ay, az


def main():
    pipeline = AccelerometerPipeline(feature_window=50, anomaly_zscore_threshold=3.0)

    while True:
        ax, ay, az = read_accelerometer()
        result = pipeline.process_sample(ax, ay, az)

        if result["anomaly"]:
            print(
                "ANOMALY DETECTED:",
                f"z={result['zscore']:.2f}",
                f"mag={result['filtered_magnitude']:.3f}",
            )
        else:
            print(
                f"OK: mag={result['filtered_magnitude']:.3f} "
                f"z={result['zscore']:.2f}"
            )

        # Simulate sensor sampling rate
        time.sleep(0.02)  # 50 Hz


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

- **Moving average smoothing**: reduces noise.
- **Rolling anomaly detection**: compares the current feature against historical mean/std using a z-score.
- **Thresholding**: flags spikes as anomalies.

```go
package main

	"log"
	"net/http"
	"os"
	"os/signal"
	"sync/atomic"
	"syscall"
	"time"
)

var requestCount uint64

func main() {
	mux := http.NewServeMux()

	// Fast health endpoint
	mux.HandleFunc("/health", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		w.WriteHeader(http.StatusOK)
		w.Write([]byte("ok"))
	})

	// Example endpoint that simulates handling work
	mux.HandleFunc("/", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		count := atomic.AddUint64(&requestCount, 1)

		w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
		fmt.Fprintf(w, `{"message":"hello","request_count":%d}`, count)
	})

	server := &http.Server{
		Addr:              ":8080",
		Handler:           loggingMiddleware(mux),
		ReadHeaderTimeout: 5 * time.Second,
		ReadTimeout:       10 * time.Second,
		WriteTimeout:      10 * time.Second,
		IdleTimeout:       120 * time.Second,
		MaxHeaderBytes:    1 << 20, // 1 MB
	}

	// Start server in a goroutine
	go func() {
		log.Println("Server listening on :8080")
		if err := server.ListenAndServe(); err != nil && err != http.ErrServerClosed {
			log.Fatalf("ListenAndServe error: %v", err)
		}
	}()

	// Graceful shutdown on SIGINT/SIGTERM
	stop := make(chan os.Signal, 1)
	signal.Notify(stop, syscall.SIGINT, syscall.SIGTERM)
	<-stop

	log.Println("Shutting down server...")

	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 10*time.Second)
	defer cancel()

	if err := server.Shutdown(ctx); err != nil {
		log.Fatalf("Server Shutdown Failed: %v", err)
	}

	log.Println("Server exited properly")
}

func loggingMiddleware(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
	return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		start := time.Now()
		next.ServeHTTP(w, r)
		log.Printf("%s %s %s", r.Method, r.URL.Path, time.Since(start))
	})
}
```

- **Atomic counter:** safe concurrent request counting.
